summary: callableSubstitutionForm (src/callable-substitution.mts) is a real, stricter, TypeScript-symbol-resolved substitutability comparator -- exactly the kind of check that would catch a false duplication-migration candidate like the one recorded the same day in jsnode-engineering-cli's data/records (two thin wrappers with the same AST shape that delegate to different named contracts) -- but it was not wired into jsnode-engineering-cli's duplication-migration apply path, and had drifted out of this package's own public index.mts (a real breaking-export gap the publish-package operator caught on this session's patch publish; restored in this same change).
detail: duplication.mts/executable-behaviors.mts compute a loose, discovery-oriented `semanticFingerprint` (ignores local names and literal values, meant for wide recall when scanning a whole workspace for candidates). callableSubstitutionForm is a separate, much stricter comparison that resolves real TypeScript symbols (via ts.createProgram/getTypeChecker) to distinguish true local bindings from free/global/captured identifiers, and refuses (returns null) on dynamic-environment constructs (this, arguments, eval, new.target). Its own docstring already frames it as the answer to 'unlike the discovery fingerprint, this retains constants, parameter defaults, binding relationships and captured module identity' -- i.e. it reads as designed to gate an actual apply, not just widen a scan. duplication-migration.mts currently never calls it.
caveat: callableSubstitutionForm resolves each file standalone (ts.createSourceFile per call, no cross-file import resolution), so it tags every free/module-level identifier as `["capture", file, name]` -- two different files referencing what is actually the same imported binding will always compare as non-equal. Before wiring it into duplication-migration's apply path as a blanket pre-apply gate, that limitation needs a real design decision: either extend it with actual import-resolution (so a shared import target compares equal across files), or restrict its use as a gate to same-file/same-package candidates only and rely on a different, import-aware check for genuine cross-package candidates. Not attempted in this session because getting this wrong either direction has real cost: too permissive re-admits the exact incident this finding is about, too conservative makes duplication-migration refuse most real cross-package consolidations it exists to perform.
recommended_next_step: Design and implement an import-aware strict verifier (reusing callableSubstitutionForm's symbol-classification approach, extended to resolve a captured identifier's real import target across files within one ts.Program) and call it from duplication-migration's plan step for every candidate before setting applicable: true; a candidate whose implementations do not verify as substitutable moves to refusals instead of sites.
owner_note: Found while fixing the false-positive discovery-fingerprint bug from the same incident (owner instruction: 'stop cheating around what i said to do... Set up the tools'). Recorded rather than rushed, since a hasty wiring risks breaking duplication-migration's main cross-package mission.
